findings.title: Backup-code authentication can bypass password verification
findings.body: Password verification for CAL accounts is skipped whenever credentials.totpCode is nonempty. The new backup-code branch then authenticates without validating that TOTP value. A request containing an email, a valid backup code, an arbitrary totpCode such as "x", and an incorrect or empty password therefore succeeds. Require verified first-factor authentication before accepting the backup code; an unvalidated TOTP field must not exempt the request from password verification.

findings.title: Consume backup codes atomically
findings.body: Backup-code validation reads the encrypted array from the earlier user query, then replaces the entire array with an unconditional update by user ID. Two concurrent requests can both validate and authenticate with the same supposedly single-use code. Concurrent requests using different codes can also overwrite each other's changes, restoring a consumed code. Validation and consumption need an atomic conditional update or a transaction that locks the row before reading and checking the codes.

findings.title: Backup recovery is unavailable in the external-provider 2FA flow
findings.body: The new Lost access button is rendered only through TwoFactorFooter, while logins with totpEmail use ExternalTotpFooter, which contains only Cancel. A user who generates backup codes as a CAL account and later links Google or SAML retains those codes, but cannot reach the backup-code input after signing in through that provider. Posting a backup code without a TOTP code is also rejected by the external-provider guards in authorize. Wire backup recovery into the external-provider verification flow so these users can recover without their authenticator.

findings.title: Notify the caller when 2FA has actually been enabled
findings.body: After the enable endpoint succeeds, onEnable is now deferred until the custom backup-codes Close button is clicked. Dismissing the dialog through its normal onOpenChange path, such as Escape, never invokes onEnable even though 2FA is already enabled on the server. This breaks the callback contract and leaves callers relying on it uninformed about the successful change. Ensure every dismissal after successful enablement propagates that result, or synchronize the enabled state independently of closing the backup-code screen.

findings.title: Wait for clipboard success before confirming the codes were copied
findings.body: navigator.clipboard.writeText returns a promise that can reject, for example when clipboard access is denied. This handler does not await or catch it and immediately displays "Backup codes copied!" regardless of the outcome. Users can close the backup-code screen believing they copied their recovery credentials when the clipboard was never updated. Show success only after the write resolves and report copying failures.

findings.title: Keep the password visibility control keyboard-accessible
findings.body: Adding tabIndex={-1} to the shared PasswordField visibility button removes it from the keyboard focus order everywhere this component is used. Keyboard-only users can no longer reach and activate Show password or Hide password with Tab and Enter/Space, although the control remains available to mouse users. Keep this interactive control in the tab order.

findings.title: Do not override PasswordField's visibility-controlled input type
findings.body: The replacement PasswordField still receives type="password". PasswordField spreads its props after setting the input type from its visibility state, so this explicit prop overrides the computed "text" type. Clicking the new Show password control changes its icon but never reveals the password. Remove the explicit type prop here or prevent it from overriding PasswordField's internal visibility state.
